articles.title: Sob novo comando, Chile enfrenta queda do PIB e desemprego recorde | G1
articles.standfirst: O desemprego no Chile atingiu o nível recorde de 9,6%, o maior em mais de cinco anos. Os investimentos estão paralisados e a confiança dos consumidores diminuiu, em meio ao plano de austeridade fiscal do governo do presidente José Antonio Kast.
articles.summary: O desemprego no Chile atingiu o nível recorde de 9,6%, o maior em mais de cinco anos. Os investimentos estão paralisados e a confiança dos consumidores diminuiu, em meio ao plano de austeridade fiscal do governo do presidente José Antonio Kast.
articles.body:
O desemprego no Chile atingiu o nível recorde de 9,6%, o maior em mais de cinco anos — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

Falando para um grupo de empresários cristãos reunidos em um pequeno auditório, o ministro da Fazenda do Chile, Jaime Quiroz, pediu que eles evitassem o pessimismo. Para isso, ele usou citações da Bíblia e também alguns números.

A mensagem era dirigida àqueles que o conhecem há muitos anos. Quiroz desenvolveu toda a sua carreira profissional como empresário no setor privado.

"Não percam a calma, nem se desesperem", declarou ele em Santiago no início de outubro, após a publicação de uma série de indicadores fracos sobre a economia chilena.

Os investimentos produtivos, privados e públicos, apresentaram crescimento nulo no segundo trimestre deste ano, principalmente devido à queda da construção civil.

O desemprego atingiu o nível recorde de 9,6%, o maior em mais de cinco anos. E a demanda interna apresentou crescimento praticamente nulo.

O custo de vida no país aumentou em julho para 4,1%, com base nos últimos 12 meses. A alta foi impulsionada, em grande parte, pelo forte aumento do preço dos combustíveis. O Chile importa quase todo o petróleo que consome.

Já a mineração sofreu redução drástica. O país é o maior exportador de cobre do mundo.

Tudo isso ocorre no contexto de um plano de austeridade fiscal implementado pelo governo do presidente José Antonio Kast, de direita radical.

Ele chegou ao poder em março, com a promessa de reativar os investimentos e o emprego. Agora, ele enfrenta um nível de desaprovação de mais de 60%, segundo pesquisas locais.

A paralisação econômica ficou em evidência devido à queda do PIB chileno em 0,5%, no primeiro trimestre do ano, e de 0,2% no segundo, em comparação com os mesmos períodos do ano passado.

Esta é a maior retração da economia do Chile desde a pandemia de covid-19 .

O primeiro semestre de 2026 registrou a maior queda da economia chilena desde a pandemia de covid-19 — Foto: Bloomberg via Getty Images

Poucos dias depois do início da guerra no Irã, Kast assumiu a Presidência no Chile com sua própria motosserra, a fim de reduzir os gastos fiscais e levar adiante um plano de austeridade econômica que deveria impulsionar o crescimento da economia do país.

Mas o conflito no Oriente Médio fez o preço do barril de petróleo disparar.

Enquanto a maioria dos países procurava uma forma de controlar a situação, o governo chileno tomou a decisão de não intervir, deixando o custo dos combustíveis subir de acordo com o mercado.

Este episódio ficou conhecido como bencinazo ("gasolinaço", em português), causando manifestações nas ruas e indignação entre muitos cidadãos chilenos.

Com a transferência do choque petrolífero para os consumidores, o preço dos combustíveis não afetou apenas o bolso das famílias mais vulneráveis e das pequenas empresas.

A alta também foi amplificada em efeito cascata e transmitida para o restante da economia, causando aumento da inflação .

O preço dos combustíveis no Chile disparou em 2026 — Foto: Getty Images

O governo que havia acabado de tomar posse tomou esta decisão considerando que "o custo fiscal de compensar a alta dos preços era excessivo e ameaçava debilitar seus esforços para reduzir o déficit fiscal", explica à BBC News Mundo (o serviço em espanhol da BBC) o principal economista para as Américas do centro de estudos Economist Intelligence Unit, Nicolás Saldías.

"O custo político para o governo foi muito elevado, pois a popularidade de Kast caiu rapidamente e não se recuperou", explica ele.

Esta decisão "afetou a confiança dos consumidores", segundo Joan Domene, economista-chefe para a América Latina da consultoria Oxford Economics.

O preço médio que os consumidores pagam pela gasolina na bomba, calculado com base na Região Metropolitana de Santiago (a mais povoada do país), aumentou em cerca de 30% desde os dias anteriores ao início da guerra no Irã até meados de outubro. Já o preço do diesel aumentou em mais de 40%.

Os especialistas concordam que, no próximo ano, poderá haver leve desaceleração dos preços globais da energia, embora marginal.

Esta projeção é atualizada constantemente. Mas, se este cenário se mantiver e não surgirem novos contratempos, é possível que surja "uma tendência para a recuperação da economia já no primeiro trimestre do ano que vem", segundo Domene.

A mineração, especialmente de cobre, é o principal produto de exportação do Chile e um dos setores mais importantes para o crescimento econômico do país.

Por isso, a queda da mineração em agosto foi tão negativa. O índice de redução foi de cerca de 17,4%, em termos anuais.

Esta queda levou a atividade mineradora chilena ao seu nível mais baixo das últimas três décadas.

O mês de agosto marcou o nível mínimo, mas a baixa produção de cobre vinha apresentando tendência negativa ao longo do ano. Acrescente-se a isso as interrupções operacionais nas minas e condições climáticas muito adversas, em julho e agosto.

No momento, as projeções indicam que a produção mineradora deverá aumentar no próximo ano, colaborando para a reativação econômica do país.

Mas uma das preocupações do setor é que a concentração de cobre nas rochas diminuiu, elevando os custos de produção e gerando incertezas.

A drástica queda da mineração em agosto levou o Banco Central chileno a reduzir as projeções de crescimento econômico deste ano, para o nível de 0,25% a 0,75%. O Fundo Monetário Internacional (FMI) também reduziu sua estimativa para 0,6%.

Se as estimativas se concretizarem, o Chile será um dos países com menor crescimento da América Latina em 2026. O único país com prognóstico inferior na região é a Bolívia.

A percepção econômica dos consumidores chilenos se deteriorou, segundo o Índice de Percepção da Economia (Ipec) de setembro — Foto: Bloomberg via Getty Images

Parte do debate no Chile se concentra em saber se a paralisação econômica é transitória ou se irá se prolongar ao longo do tempo.

Desde que Kast assumiu o poder, um dos seus principais focos no setor econômico tem sido a austeridade fiscal.

Suas medidas incluíram o corte de 3% do orçamento de todos os ministérios , uma controversa redução ou fechamento de programas considerados "ineficientes" pelo governo e a redução dos investimentos públicos diretos.

Neste sentido, Nicolás Saldías destaca que as políticas fiscais do governo chileno "também estão reduzindo o crescimento econômico".

O governo conseguiu reduzir o déficit, em parte, graças à redução dos gastos públicos, o que diminui a demanda da economia, segundo o economista.

Com a bandeira do ajuste fiscal nas mãos, o governo chileno apresentou a chamada "megarreforma", um pacote de medidas propostas para o Congresso . Elas foram apresentadas como estímulo ao crescimento econômico e aos investimentos.

Basicamente, o pacote inclui uma reforma tributária que, entre outros pontos, reduz progressivamente os impostos para as empresas, de 27% para cerca de 23%, e garante invariabilidade tributária a longo prazo para os grandes investimentos.

O Congresso aprovou a megarreforma, que foi sancionada pelo presidente Kast no início de outubro, após árduos debates. A questão é se a redução de impostos corporativos e os outros incentivos para investimentos produzirão crescimento e empregos em níveis suficientes para compensar a queda da arrecadação fiscal.

Enquanto as medidas começam a ser implementadas e à luz dos indicadores existentes no momento, Joan Domene defende que o próximo ano deve trazer "uma reversão de muitos dos fatores causadores de incertezas".

O economista para a América Latina da Bloomberg Intelligence, Felipe Hernández, é da mesma opinião.

Para ele, se as reformas forem implementadas e cumprirem efetivamente as previsões do governo, como esperam as empresas, "poderemos começar a observar efeitos positivos na economia no próximo ano".

As previsões indicam melhoria da situação econômica chilena em 2027 — Foto: AFP via Getty Images

Atualmente, o Congresso chileno está discutindo a Lei Orçamentária para 2027. Ela contempla um crescimento real dos gastos públicos de apenas 1,5%, um objetivo considerado austero em comparação com os governos anteriores.

A oposição vem questionando duramente este projeto. Ela denuncia que a proposta afeta dezenas de programas sociais que beneficiam pessoas vulneráveis, mas que o governo considera que não atingem os seus objetivos.

Em meio a esta situação , grande parte da população está frustrada com o desempenho econômico do país, segundo as pesquisas.

Com a alta da inflação e o desemprego em máximos históricos, muitos cidadãos enfrentam dificuldades na sua vida diária.

O consumo geral das famílias chilenas cresce lentamente e o Índice de Vendas de Supermercados fechou agosto em queda de 1,2% nos últimos 12 meses, segundo o Instituto Nacional de Estatísticas.

Algumas semanas atrás, o governo anunciou um plano de emprego de cerca de US$ 1,3 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,5 trilhões). O objetivo é criar mais de 100 mil postos de trabalho entre 2026 e 2027, acelerando obras públicas e oferecendo subsídios às empresas, para incentivar contratações.

Este tipo de plano não fazia parte da política de austeridade adotada pelo governo chileno, quando assumiu o poder em março. Mas, frente às circunstâncias, se o anúncio for cumprido, poderá dar oxigênio à economia do país.

articles.title: Woman claims Rs 14.70 lakh Section 54F tax exemption for flat; taxman denies saying she has many properties, but ITAT gives relief as one was company-owned and another jointly owned with husband
articles.summary: You own a house and claim exemption under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act.
articles.body: You own a house and claim exemption under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act. However, the exemption is denied because the Income Tax Department believes you own more than one property.In one such case, the dispute arose because the income tax department considered that the woman owned more than one house property, making her ineligible for the deduction.However, in its order pronounced on September 10, 2026, the tribunal allowed her appeal and reversed the decision of the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals).Also Read | Cook working in a 5-star hotel gets Rs 4 crore tax notice with penalty for alleged Rs 24.62 crore sales, but he claims PAN was misused which led to wrong Form 26AS entry; why Delhi HC gave reliefWhat the case is aboutThe Income Tax Department reopened a woman’s assessment for assessment year 2015-16, alleging that she had wrongly claimed a Rs 14.70 lakh deduction under Section 54F of the Income Tax Act.The Assessing Officer denied the deduction on the ground that she owned more than one residential house apart from the new asset, and assessed her income at Rs 16,70,500.The woman challenged the assessment before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), National Faceless Appeal Centre, but her appeal was dismissed on August 20, 2025.The assessment proceedings referred to three properties in Nagpur. The question before the tribunal was whether the ownership of the other properties meant she failed to meet the conditions for claiming the benefit.The tribunal described the dispute as follows: “The sole grievance of the assessee is against the deduction u/s.54F of the Act by the Revenue authorities alleging that assessee owned more than one house property making the assessee disentitled for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act.”Also Read | Husband and wife sell property; Income Tax dept alleges Rs 3.30 crore sale against Rs 1.60 crore in deed, cites WhatsApp chats, Excel sheets to claim Rs 1.70 crore cash receipts, but ITAT gives reliefWhy did ITAT rule in favour of the home owner?The tribunal examined three properties mentioned in the assessment proceedings and found that one belonged to a company in which the woman was a director, while another was jointly owned by her and her husband.It held that the company's property could not be treated as her personally owned property merely because of her association with the company.The flat was jointly owned by the woman and her husband, although she had not contributed towards its purchase.The order records: “So far as the third property, the same is jointly owned by the assessee and her husband and the assessee has not provided any amount towards the purchase of the said property.”The tribunal concluded that the woman fulfilled the conditions for claiming the deduction, stating: “The assessee has fulfilled the necessary conditions for claiming deduction u/s.54F of the Act and therefore entitled to deduction u/s.54F of the Act at Rs 14,70,000/-.”Also Read | Woman applied for 130 IPO shares, bank entered only 65; consumer commission awards Rs 37,000 for deficient service but rejects her Rs 40 lakh compensation claimThe order identifies one house property owned by the woman for the purpose of its conclusion.The tribunal reversed the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals)’s finding, stating: “Finding of ld.CIT(A) is reversed.” It allowed the woman’s grounds of appeal and concluded: “In the result, the appeal of the assessee is allowed.”The tribunal thus granted the Rs 14.70 lakh deduction after examining the specific property-ownership facts before it.Kuldip Kumar, Partner at Mainstay Tax Advisors LLP notes that owning more than one residential house is one of the most common grounds on which tax authorities deny exemption under Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961.In this case, the tax authorities considered three properties while denying the exemption. The ITAT observed that one property was owned by a company in which the taxpayer was a director and, therefore, could not be treated as her property merely because of her directorship.The second property was the new house acquired for claiming the Section 54F exemption and was consequently excluded from the count.The third property was jointly owned by the taxpayer and her husband. Although the taxpayer had not contributed towards its purchase, the Tribunal treated her as a joint owner of that property.The Tribunal concluded that the taxpayer owned only one residential house other than the new asset and, therefore, fulfilled the relevant ownership condition for claiming the exemption under Section 54F.“There have been several favourable judicial decisions in which appellate authorities have held that fractional or joint ownership of residential properties should not necessarily be equated with exclusive ownership for determining eligibility under Section 54F,” he tells TOI.In some cases, taxpayers have been allowed to claim the exemption despite holding fractional interests in multiple residential properties.Also Read | He inherited land from mother, redeveloped home & received Rs 75 lakh from builder; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT Delhi gives relief, ruling multiple floors can qualify as one houseSignificance of rulingAccording to Kuldip Kumar, this ITAT ruling highlights the importance of examining the facts and ownership of each property before determining eligibility for the exemption.“Joint ownership of residential property, particularly between spouses, is common. It may arise from inheritance, estate planning, the desire to avoid future family disputes or the need to ensure that the surviving spouse can manage the property without unnecessary complications,” he adds.“For taxpayers claiming exemption under Section 86 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (corresponding to Section 54F of the Income-tax Act, 1961), these favourable judicial precedents may provide support where jointly owned properties are involved. However, the outcome will depend on the facts of each case and the judicial precedents applicable to it, and the possibility of the tax authorities taking a contrary view cannot be ruled out,” Kumar tells TOI.“A legislative clarification specifying how jointly owned or fractional interests in residential properties should be counted for the purposes of this provision would provide greater certainty, reduce litigation and benefit taxpayers at large,” he adds.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claimYou use AI every day. articles.title: Oil prices today: Brent crude tops $110 as Middle East tensions threaten shipments
articles.summary: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed concerns over Middle East supplies amid growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea and threats to oil
articles.body: Oil prices rose on Wednesday as traders weighed concerns over Middle East supplies amid growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea and threats to oil infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.Brent crude futures climbed $1.34, or 1.23 per cent, to $110.10 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose $1.18, or 1.21 per cent, to $99 per barrel.The gains followed a decline in the previous session, when prices eased after Iran's president discussed mediation efforts with Pakistan's army chief during a meeting in Tehran.Tanker attacks raise concerns over oil suppliesSupply concerns intensified after a supertanker caught fire after striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy.Iranian media reported that the vessel had been “violating” Iranian regulations.At least 18 vessel attacks were reported over a two-week period, ship-tracking firm Kpler said in a note on Monday.The attacks have also spread beyond the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil shipments.“Attacks on tankers have expanded beyond the Strait of Hormuz,” LSEG analysts said in a note.“Iran has been targeting vessels as far south as the Gulf of Oman, threatening loadings outside of the Arab Gulf, as well as the ship-to-ship transfers that have helped to support Middle East loadings as the conflict has dragged on,” the analysts added.The Houthis on Monday claimed responsibility for attacks on a Saudi Aramco site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield and the airports in Riyadh and Abha, Saudi Arabia.Meanwhile, the death toll from a Houthi attack on Yemeni government forces on Monday rose to 73 as fighting intensified, Reuters reported.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said in a television interview aired on Tuesday that Tehran had not received a response from Saudi Arabia or Yemen's Houthis to its offer to help broker peace talks.Oil prices retreat from five-month highDespite Wednesday's gains, crude prices had fallen in the previous session after reaching elevated levels.Brent crude futures settled down 76 cents, or 0.69 per cent, at $108.79 per barrel on Tuesday, after touching a five-month high of $111.99.The November contract for US WTI crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled $1.87 lower, down 1.8 per cent, at $101.79 per barrel.US works to increase fuel suppliesIn the United States, two Energy Department officials said on Tuesday that they were working with refiners around the world to increase fuel production as a diesel shortage pushed prices higher.US crude oil inventories were also expected to have declined in the week ended October 16, alongside stocks of refined petroleum products, according to an extended Reuters poll.The eight analysts surveyed by Reuters estimated that US crude inventories fell by an average of around 800,000 barrels during the week.Market participants are monitoring developments across the Middle East, including threats to shipping routes and energy articles.title: India-US ‘pretty close’ to signing a ‘different kind of deal,’ says Donald Trump
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) said India and the United States were “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal after more than a year
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) said India and the United States were “pretty close” to finalising a trade deal after more than a year of negotiations. He further added that the agreement “could be a much different kind of deal”.“They want to make a deal. We’re going to make a deal. Pretty close, yeah,” Trump told reporters at the White House when asked about the prospects of an agreement. His remarks come amid growing optimism on both sides over the long-pending deal, with US secretary of state Marco Rubio also describing it as “incredibly close” during his visit to India.Rubio and external affairs minister S Jaishankar held wide-ranging discussions in Mumbai on Tuesday, reviewing the full scope of India-US relations and committing to an early conclusion of the proposed Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).The meeting took place against the backdrop of the US Freedom 250 Reception hosted by US ambassador to India Sergio Gor in Mumbai. The ministry of external affairs (MEA) said that the discussions covered key strategic sectors, including trade, defence, technology and energy security. "They welcomed the progress made in negotiations on the India–US Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) and reaffirmed their commitment to working towards its early conclusion," the MEA stated.The ministry added that Rubio's visit reflected "the sustained momentum of high-level exchanges between the two countries, underscoring the importance both sides attach to further advancing the India-US COMPACT for the 21st century."Rubio is on an official visit to India from October 20 to 21 at Jaishankar's invitation. The trip marks his second visit to the country, following an earlier trip to New Delhi in May. He will next travel to Jamnagar in Gujarat for discussions that will include "enhanced energy cooperation", according to the US state department.Rubio calls India-US alignment ‘extraordinary’Earlier on Tuesday, Rubio described the strategic alignment between India and the United States as “extraordinary”, saying the two countries had an opportunity to shape the course of the 21st century through their partnership.Speaking at the Freedom 250 Reception in Mumbai, he acknowledged that the two countries would not agree on every issue but said their shared interests could shape geopolitics, economics, trade and commerce for decades.“No two nations on Earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue, and there will be times and points of disagreement,” Rubio stated. “But on the core issues that matter, the core issues that define the national interests of both India and the United States, the alignment between our countries is extraordinary,” he added.Rubio also said the United States should engage diplomatically with India more frequently, describing the country as one of Washington's most important geopolitical partners.Explaining the significance of his Mumbai visit, Rubio highlighted the city's role as India's financial and commercial hub, with many companies investing in and trading with the United States based there.US, India officials express optimism over negotiationsTrump's comments follow recent positive assessments from officials in both countries about the prospects of an agreement after a prolonged stalemate over trade between Washington and New Delhi.Last week, Gor told the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi that the “the big items are done” and that the two countries were very close to “landing it.”Jaishankar had also said he was “encouraged” by progress in the trade talks, adding that both sides were “heading toward a landing point.”The negotiations have also unfolded against the backdrop of Trump's decision late Friday to articles.title: Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know
articles.summary: Jio Platforms IPO: India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday.
articles.body: Jio Platforms IPO: India’s largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) till date opens for subscription on Wednesday. Jio Platforms plans to raise approximately Rs 30,213 crore through a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares.The public issue opens on October 21 and will remain available for subscription until October 23. This marks RIL Group's first IPO in nearly two decades.Reliance Industries Ltd, led by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, will continue to hold a majority stake in Jio Platforms following its stock market listing.From Jio IPO price band, listing date to GMP, we take a look at 10 important facts about the Jio IPO and what brokerages are saying:Jio IPO price bandThe company has fixed the price band at Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 per share. Based on the offer documents, the IPO values the company at around $108 billion. Investors will be able to apply for Jio Platforms shares in lots of 12, or in multiples of 12 shares.The company is also seeking to widen access to its IPO by setting aside portions of the issue for different investor groups.Eligible Reliance Industries shareholders have a reservation of up to Rs 2,500 crore, while eligible employees can apply under a reservation of up to Rs 500 crore. Retail individual investors will be eligible to subscribe to at least 35 per cent of the net offer.Jio IPO listing dateJio Platforms will list on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) on October 28, 2026.India’s largest IPOThe Jio IPO is expected to surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,870 crore IPO in 2024, making it the largest public issue in India's history by value.The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares, meaning existing shareholders are not selling their holdings through the offering.Jio IPO GMPJio’s shares are trading at a grey market premium (GMP) of around 22%, signalling strong interest. On Tuesday, October 20, Jio Platforms shares were quoting at a grey market premium of about Rs 245.GMP refers to the premium that speculators in the unofficial market are prepared to pay for shares of a company awaiting its IPO listing.Based on the upper end of the IPO price band of Rs 1,119, this indicates a possible listing price of Rs 1,364, implying a premium of nearly 22%, according to unofficial grey market quotes.Jio set to be fourth most valuable listed company?Based on the current market capitalisation rankings on the BSE, the company would become India's fourth-most valuable listed company. It would rank behind RIL, valued at Rs 15.9 lakh crore, Bharti Airtel at Rs 11.2 lakh crore and HDFC Bank at nearly Rs 11 lakh crore.The BSE data also showed that Jio Platforms' valuation would be higher than those of ICICI Bank, State Bank of India and TCS.Reliance could topple Tata as India's most valuable groupAccording to this TOI report, Reliance Industries (RIL) Group is poised to displace Tata Group as India's most valuable conglomerate once Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut, marking one of the biggest changes in the country's corporate pecking order in decades.At the upper end of its proposed price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 per share, Jio Platforms is expected to command a valuation of Rs 10.3 lakh crore. This would take the combined market capitalisation of the RIL Group to around Rs 28.5 lakh crore, putting it ahead of Tata Group's Rs 25.5 lakh crore as of October 15, according to ET Intelligence data.Before the proposed listing, RIL Group's market capitalisation stood at Rs 18.2 lakh crore.Adani Group currently occupies the third position among India's largest conglomerates, with a market capitalisation of Rs 17.48 lakh crore. It is followed by HDFC Group at Rs 13.91 lakh crore and Bajaj Group at Rs 13.88 lakh crore.What Akash Ambani saidJio Platforms expects technology, artificial intelligence and cloud computing to fuel its next phase of expansion beyond telecom, Managing Director Akash Ambani told PTI."There is no either-or at Jio: the network is our technology," Ambani said in an interview with PTI. He pointed to the company's in-house 5G core, cloud-native radio access network and software platform, which serves 533.3 million customers.Satellite connectivity and next-generation 6G technology are among the other areas Jio has identified for future development.According to Ambani, the company's growth prospects are spread across several segments, from mobile services and home broadband to digital solutions for enterprises. He noted that around 26 crore Indians continue to use 2G services, while fixed broadband is available in only about 21 per cent of households across the country.About JioIn the decade since Reliance entered the telecom sector, Jio Platforms has built a subscriber base that places it among the world's largest mobile operators.Its operations now extend well beyond mobile connectivity, covering broadband, digital entertainment, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio Platforms recorded revenue from operations of Rs 1.46 lakh crore in FY26, up from Rs 1.28 lakh crore in FY25. Net profit climbed to Rs 30,049 crore from Rs 26,109 crore over the same period, while EBITDA grew to Rs 76,255 crore from Rs 64,170 crore.Company figures reported for June 2026 show that Jio Platforms had 533.3 million subscribers and accounted for nearly 60% of India's data traffic.The IPO is also expected to improve Jio's financial position. The company plans to use up to Rs 27,500 crore of the net proceeds to repay or prepay borrowings owed by its telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm.Jio's net debt-to-EBITDA ratio fell to 0.36 times in FY26, compared with 0.88 times in FY24, Akash Ambani said. He added that the IPO would give the company more financial headroom to invest in areas such as 5G, broadband, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and enterprise services.Jio's international technology investors, including Google and Meta, are also expected to contribute to its next stage of growth.Anchor bookJio Platforms has allotted shares worth Rs 8,109.85 crore to 212 anchor investors at Rs 1,119 apiece, which is the upper end of its IPO’s price band.Institutional bids for the offering crossed a whopping Rs 2.5 lakh crore, which is more than 30 times the value of shares on offer in the anchor book.The company has allocated 7.24 crore shares.The scale of demand points to strong institutional interest in what is expected to be India's largest IPO.Life Insurance Corporation of India was the biggest recipient in the anchor allotment, securing shares worth Rs 499.98 crore. New World Fund Inc received shares of Rs 486.27 crore, while the Government of Singapore was allotted Rs 340.93 crore.SBI Focused Fund secured an allocation worth Rs 315 crore, followed by BNP Paribas Financial Markets - ODI, which received shares valued at Rs 303.25 crore.Domestic mutual funds were allotted 2.489 crore shares worth Rs 2,784.96 crore, which is 34.34% of the anchor book.Several major international investment firms also participated in the anchor book. These included BlackRock, Capital Group, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, Schroders, JPMorgan Asset Management, Franklin Templeton and Janus Henderson.What brokerages are sayingBrokerages have expressed optimism about the offering, pointing to Jio's leading position in the telecom sector, improving profitability and potential for expansion in broadband and artificial intelligence.Motilal Oswal Wealth Management has advised investors to subscribe to the Jio IPO, citing potential listing gains as well as long-term investment prospects. The brokerage pointed to the company's strong position in India's telecom market and its improving earnings performance. It said Jio's extensive subscriber base, in-house technology capabilities and growing broadband business offer a solid platform for further expansion.The brokerage noted that Jio had 533 million subscribers as of June 2026 and accounted for around 60% of India's wireless data traffic. It also sees scope for growth in digital services, backed by Jio's proprietary 5G technology, more than 7,200 patent applications and investments in cloud computing and artificial intelligence.Canara Bank Securities has also recommended subscribing to the issue with a long-term investment horizon. According to the brokerage, Jio stands to gain as customers shift from 2G to 4G and 5G services, home broadband adoption expands and the company explores opportunities to monetise its technology in international markets.Canara Bank Securities identified Jio's in-house technology portfolio, spanning its 5G network, broadband solutions and JioBrain AI platform, as potential drivers of future revenue growth.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX and Tesla exploring largest merger in history
articles.summary: Tech mogul says tie-up has a ‘lot of merit’, given firms’ complementary work on AI.
articles.body:
Elon Musk has revealed that SpaceX and Tesla are exploring a possible merger, a tie-up that would create a corporate colossus worth more than $3 trillion.

Musk said on Tuesday that his two largest companies had established special committees to explore a merger.

The SpaceX and Tesla CEO said the idea had a “lot of merit”, given the companies’ complementary work on artificial intelligence, but the committees had not come to any agreement on a proposal.

“They’ve got to come up with something, and then that’s got to be put to the shareholders as a vote,” Musk said on a SpaceX earnings call.

Musk, the world’s richest man with a net worth of more than $900bn, said that a merger would need to clear the “high hurdle” of a 50 percent vote among Tesla shareholders

“Some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” Musk said.

“Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes. But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this.”

A SpaceX-Tesla merger would rank as the biggest corporate tie-up in history, far exceeding the $1.25 trillion union between SpaceX and xAI in February.

At current valuations, SpaceX and Tesla rank as the world’s seventh- and eleventh-largest companies, respectively, with a combined market capitalisation of about $3.5 trillion.

Jerayr Haleblian, an expert in mergers and acquisitions at the University of California, Riverside, said a SpaceX-Tesla merger has “sound logic” to support it.

“In some sense, the core of both businesses are expert manufacturing. From a technology transfer perspective, there should be significant flows of information between businesses,” Haleblian told Al Jazeera.

“Both firms seem to have expertise in robotics, AI, energy infrastructure,” he said.

“Accordingly, the core skills are applicable across industry sectors. The key to success will be synergistic innovation, which I anticipate will follow from acquisition.”

Shares of SpaceX, which went public in June in the largest Initial Public Offering (IPO) of all time, rose more than 8 percent in after-hours trading following Musk’s comments.

Musk’s comments came as SpaceX on Tuesday reported its first quarterly profit, driven by strong growth in its AI and satellite-internet divisions.

Net profit was $4.4bn in the July-September quarter, a reversal from a $1.05bn net loss a year earlier.

Profit in the first three quarters totalled $413m, versus a loss of $2.59bn during the same period a year earlier.

articles.title: 24 million barrels a day: Gulf oil flows surge past prewar levels despite US-Iran war
articles.summary: Persian Gulf oil exports have climbed above prewar levels despite intensifying attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as tankers adapt to the risks
articles.body: Persian Gulf oil exports have climbed above prewar levels despite intensifying attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, as tankers adapt to the risks with US protection and alternative routes help keep supplies moving.Oil flows from the Middle East, including shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and alternative routes, averaged more than 24 million barrels a day in the week ending October 18, exceeding the prewar average of 23.3 million barrels a day, according to ship-tracking firm Kpler.However, shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remain below their earlier levels. Preliminary estimates put average flows through the strait, including offshore transfers in the Gulf of Oman, at around 14 million barrels a day during the same period, about 82% of prewar volumes, the Wall Stree Journal reported.The recovery comes as the risks to shipping remain high. Around 30 attacks on vessels have been reported in October, accounting for about 20% of all ship attacks recorded during the war, according to Michelle Wiese Bockmann, a senior analyst at maritime intelligence firm Windward.How oil is moving despite the attacksAn improvised shipping system, supported by US protection, has helped tankers continue carrying crude through the high-risk waterway. Some vessels make short trips into the Gulf to load oil before travelling through Hormuz and transferring their cargo to other ships near Oman for onward delivery.Tankers often switch off their tracking signals during parts of these journeys. American air cover provides some protection along a corridor near the Omani coast, although vessels remain vulnerable to attacks.Pipelines running across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates are also helping exporters bypass the strait. Around 40% of non-Iranian crude shipped out of the Gulf in September travelled through routes that avoided Hormuz, compared with 17% before the war, Kpler estimated.“The big picture is that the system for shipping through a dangerous Strait of Hormuz is now well-established and the risk appetite of those involved in exporting oil has risen,” said Hamad Hussain, a senior commodities economist at Capital Economics.The increased willingness to take risks is partly driven by the potential returns. Traders can earn around $20 more per barrel by reselling Iraqi oil than before the war, according to Homayoun Falakshahi, Kpler's head of crude oil analysis. That translates into an additional $40 million on a supertanker carrying a typical cargo of two million barrels.Shipowners are also offering higher payments to attract crews willing to make the dangerous crossings. One China-based ship-staffing company offered seafarers as much as $25,000 for a round trip that typically takes one or two weeks, The Wall Street Journal reported.“The volumes remain high despite rising attacks, because profits make it worth the risk,” Falakshahi said.Attacks raise the cost of shippingThe continued movement of oil has not made the route safe. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has used drones and missiles against vessels attempting the crossing, while small boats have also been used to target shipping.The risks were illustrated by the Tanzania-flagged supertanker "Loyalty", which entered the Persian Gulf twice in September and October to load Iraqi crude. After transferring two million barrels of oil to another tanker in the Gulf of Oman in early October, it returned to the Gulf for another cargo.On October 16, the vessel was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat, maritime security company Vanguard said. The projectile damaged a freshwater tank while the tanker was carrying two million barrels of Iraqi crude, according to a crew member.The danger has pushed up the cost of transporting oil. Freight for a supertanker carrying Gulf crude to China approached a record $37.37 per barrel this week, Kpler said. War-risk insurance premiums have risen to as much as 10% of a vessel's value, from less than 3% before the conflict, according to Windward.“In April, the problem was a shortage of crude. In October, it is the cost of moving it,” said Natasha Kaneva, head of the global commodities strategy team at JPMorgan.Brent crude rose to around $108 a barrel on Tuesday, reflecting concerns that the improvement in oil flows may not last if fighting intensifies again. With global inventories thinning, any renewed disruption could leave markets with limited room to absorb a supply shock.Iran's leverage over oil flows weakensThe recovery in regional exports contrasts with the pressure on Iran's own oil trade, which has been constrained by a US maritime blockade.Tehran has sought to reassert control over Hormuz, warning that neighbouring countries should not be able to export oil if Iran cannot ship its own. But the continued movement of crude through the strait and alternative routes has weakened its ability to deter regional shipments.“Iran would have to be more aggressive to achieve the same degree of control it previously possessed over oil flows from the region,” Hussain said.That leaves the market facing two competing realities: oil exports have recovered beyond prewar levels, but the cost and danger of moving crude remain elevated. Whether the recovery can be sustained will depend on the security of shipping routes and whether the conflict escalates further.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: AI boom set to push Big Tech investment beyond $1 trillion in 2027, says UBS
articles.summary: Big tech firms are set to splurge over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027 as demand for computing power continues to grow faster than supply,
articles.body: Big tech firms are set to splurge over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure in 2027 as demand for computing power continues to grow faster than supply, according to a report by UBS.The investment boom is also helping boost US economic growth, even as companies face rising funding needs. Spending on AI infrastructure is expected to cross $600 billion in 2026 before topping $1 trillion in 2027, the report stated.“Demand has exceeded capacity ahead of schedule,” UBS said, pointing to the growing pressure on companies to expand their computing infrastructure to keep up with demand.It expects spending to rise further over the next year, although the pace of growth could peak in 2027. Higher investment is putting pressure on companies’ cash flows and increasing their need for additional funding.AI spending supports US economic growthThe growing investment in AI infrastructure has become a significant contributor to the US economy. According to UBS, spending on AI infrastructure added around 0.75 percentage points to US gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the first half of 2026.Rising equity prices linked to AI companies have also boosted household wealth and consumption, providing another source of support for economic activity.However, the report found little clear evidence that AI has so far led to a substantial increase in overall productivity or widespread job displacement. Its estimated effect on the overall unemployment rate remains limited, at around 0.2 percentage points or less.The impact on employment has varied across industries. Selected high-technology sectors, including software and computer systems design, recorded a 1.4 per cent year-on-year decline in employment. In contrast, construction industries supporting data centre infrastructure saw employment grow by nearly 3 per cent.Rising investment puts pressure on cash flowsWhile demand for AI infrastructure continues to drive investment, UBS has flagged emerging financing pressures among major technology companies. Their cash flows have weakened as spending has increased, while demand for their bond issuances has become less robust.The report said investors expect free cash flow to return to positive territory in 2028, provided companies are able to generate sufficient revenue from AI services.The ability to convert heavy infrastructure spending into sustainable revenue will therefore remain important as the investment cycle progresses.AI demand is also contributing to higher prices in some areas, including software, digital goods and electricity, according to UBS. However, the report noted that productivity gains from AI could help reduce inflation over time.The outlook for the investment cycle will depend on whether demand for computing power continues to exceed available capacity and whether technology companies can turn their growing investments into sustainable revenue growth.You use AI every day. articles.title: OpenAI says its agents turned off own safeguards
articles.summary: ChatGPT creator says AI agents disabled misalignment monitoring during two internal coding tasks.
articles.body:
OpenAI has revealed that its AI agents disabled monitoring for unsanctioned behaviour during internal use in the latest incident of the frontier technology going rogue.

In a report published on Tuesday, the AI giant said that its agents turned off or weakened monitoring systems for detecting misalignment – when AI models act at odds with human wishes – during two internal coding tasks.

The incidents involved a GPT-6.1 Sol agent disabling automatic alerts to the company’s security team, and a GPT-6 Astra agent removing a monitoring system and falsely claiming it had not done so, OpenAI said.

The ChatGPT creator said neither case met the threshold for a highest-priority incident necessitating immediate review by its security team.

OpenAI said it updated its systems to better detect attempts to disable misalignment monitoring and began investigating the cause.

“It is possible that this behavior is simply an example of ‘benign’ overpersistence, with models not understanding why monitoring is important or insisting that instructions be executed beyond what a reasonable person might expect,” the San Francisco-based firm said.

“We are also developing evaluations to test whether models might have a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring in particular and exhibit motivated reasoning in order to do so.”

Roman V Yampolskiy, an expert on AI and cybersecurity at the University of Louisville, described the revelations as “extremely concerning, but not surprising.”

“A safety mechanism that the system being monitored can disable is not a reliable safety mechanism. Particularly concerning is that one agent subsequently denied removing the monitor,” Yampolskiy told Al Jazeera.

“Monitoring cannot guarantee safety if the monitored system can undermine the monitor,” Yampolskiy said.

“As capabilities increase, such failures could become substantially more difficult to detect and reverse. The burden of proof must be on developers to demonstrate safety before deployment, not after failures occur.”

Rogue behaviour by AI models has been under heightened scrutiny since July, when OpenAI revealed that some of its agents broke out of a controlled testing environment and hacked the AI platform Hugging Face.

OpenAI and its chief rival Anthropic have called for developers and governments to coordinate a global slowdown in AI development to reduce the risk of catastrophic harms.

The US and China, the world’s leading AI powers, have displayed little appetite for cooperation on AI regulation, with coordination so far limited to pledges to improve communication on incidents with implications for safety or national security.

articles.title: Retired PSU bank employee claimed Rs 9.29 lakh leave encashment as tax-free, but taxman restricted exemption to Rs 3 lakh; ITAT applies Rs 25 lakh limit retrospectively, cancels Rs 6.29 lakh addition
articles.summary: Leave encashment is tax-free up to a limit for non-government employees. While the limit was earlier Rs 3 lakh, it was revised to Rs 25 lakh in 2023.
articles.body: Leave encashment is tax-free up to a limit for non-government employees. While the limit was earlier Rs 3 lakh, it was revised to Rs 25 lakh in 2023. There is no such upper limit for government employees. What happens if you don’t know the limit and do not pay tax on your leave encashment.In one such case a retired employee of State Bank of India (SBI) got leave encashment but did not pay tax.What the case is aboutUnder income tax law, SBI staff are treated as non-government employees and, therefore, can claim leave encashment exemption subject to the applicable limit.A retired SBI employee from Jaipur, was unaware of this distinction. When he retired in 2020 he received Rs 9.29 lakh as leave encashment and did not pay tax on the amount.Also Read | Man sold his house and bought a Rs 1.10 crore flat jointly with wife; income tax department denies Rs 55.48 lakh capital gains exemption for half the amount, but ITAT Mumbai gives full reliefAt that time, the exemption limit was Rs 3 lakh. It was subsequently increased to Rs 25 lakh in 2023 through Notification No. S.O. 2276(E).Under the limit applicable when the man retired, he would technically have been liable to pay tax on Rs 6.29 lakh, the amount that exceeded the Rs 3 lakh exemption.The man filed his income tax return (ITR) declaring total income of Rs 6.76 lakh from pension and other sources. In the return, he claimed an exemption of the entire Rs 9.29 lakh received as leave encashment under Section 10(10AA), which covers the cash equivalent of leave salary received at retirement.When the Income Tax Assessing Officer (AO) processed his return, the claim was restricted to Rs 3 lakh. The officer added the remaining Rs 6.29 lakh to Gupta's taxable income, taking his total income to Rs 13.05 lakh, according to an ET report on the judgement.The Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals), or CIT(A), upheld the adjustment, relying on the Delhi High Court's judgment in Kamal Kumar Kalia v. Union of India [2020] 268 Taxman 398 (Delhi).The man however appealed before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Jaipur.On September 22, 2026, the ITAT Jaipur ruled in the retired bank employee’s favour.Also Read | She bought shares for Rs 13.5 lakh and sold them for Rs 77.47 lakh after 18 months; taxman denied capital gains exemption, but ITAT gives relief and deletes Rs 79 lakh in additionsWhy did the retired bank employee get tax relief from ITAT?The Jaipur tax tribunal noted that the distinction between government employees and other employees under clause (10AA) of Section 10 had been upheld by the Delhi High Court in Kamal Kumar Kalia (supra). The High Court had ruled that employees of public sector undertakings and nationalised banks could not claim the same status as government employees for this purpose.The ITAT Jaipur observed that the revised leave encashment exemption limit of Rs 25 lakh took effect from April 1, 2023, following the notification issued on May 24, 2023.According to the tribunal, the 2023 revision did not amount to the introduction of a new exemption. Instead, it was the belated fulfilment of an obligation, as the exemption ceiling had remained at Rs 3 lakh since 2002 despite successive revisions to salaries.ITAT Jaipur observed: “A notification of that character is remedial, and to withhold its benefit from an employee who retired shortly before it was issued would perpetuate the very disparity it was meant to remove.”Also Read | Rs 5.89 crore FD interest slashed from 7.75% to 3.5% without notice; Delhi High Court rejects bank’s non-renewal argument and orders interest at an average of earlier ratesThe tribunal also noted that its Coordinate Benches had consistently adopted the same approach in cases involving retired bank employees. These included Dashrath Kumar Sen v. ACIT [2025] 172 taxmann.com 772 (Jaipur - Trib.), which dealt with the same assessment year, AY 2020-21, and Govind Chhatwani v. CIT (Appeals) [2026] 187 taxmann.com 389 (Jaipur - Trib.).The tribunal said: “The amount of Rs 9,29,033 received by him is well within the limit of Rs 25,00,000, and no other limit prescribed by the sub-clause has been applied against him.”Accordingly, the ITAT directed the Assessing Officer (AO) to allow the full exemption of Rs 9,29,033 under Section 10(10AA) and delete the addition of Rs 6,29,033.Also Read | Grandmother and her son gifted 2.5-acre land to his second wife, who sold it; his daughter from first marriage claimed it was ancestral, but Madras HC rejects her pleaChartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the Jaipur Bench of the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) extended the enhanced Rs 25 lakh exemption limit for leave encashment to a retired State Bank of India employee, even though his case concerned assessment year 2020-21, before the statutory limit was raised in 2023.Surana points out that the tribunal did not classify SBI employees as equivalent to Central or State Government employees. It made clear that staff working for public-sector undertakings and nationalised banks are not eligible for the unlimited leave encashment tax exemption available to government employees.The ITAT Jaipur held that denying the revised benefit to someone who had retired shortly before the higher limit was notified would continue the very disparity that the change was intended to address.You use AI every day. articles.title: Santiago Niño Becerra, economista, carga contra el cambio de hora: "En Vigo, igual que en Oporto, es absurdo"
articles.standfirst: La noche del 24 al 25 de octubre los relojes se atrasarán
articles.summary: La noche del 24 al 25 de octubre los relojes se atrasarán
articles.body: Santiago Niño Becerra, economista, ha analizado el cambio de hora de invierno, que se producirá este fin de semana. Concretamente, durante la madrugada del 24 al 25 de octubre, los relojes en España, a las 3:00 horas volverán a marcar las 2:00 en la Península y Baleares, mientras que en Canarias el cambio será a las 2:00, pasando a ser la 1:00. El catedrático ha analizado este movimiento. "España continuará anclada al meridiano de Berlín y no al de Greenwich, como le corresponde, como sí hace Portugal", ha comentado. Niño Becerra ha planteado que, debido a esto, se producirán situaciones que considera sorprendentes. "Por ello, en Vigo será una hora más que en Oporto", ha reflexionado en una publicación en X, antes Twitter. El catalán ha dejado muy clara su opinión sobre este movimiento: "Absurdo". Como suele ocurrir en estas plataformas, en los comentarios se han producido reacciones a favor y en contra. En 1884, en la Conferencia Internacional del Meridiano, celebrada en Washington, se acordó que el meridiano de Greenwich, o meridiano cero, era la referencia para calcular la longitud geográfica: 22 países votaron a favor, uno en contra y dos se abstuvieron. En España, Franco dictaminó, el 16 de marzo de 1940, que el país se alineara con la hora de Europa Central y con la Occidental. Algunos historiadores afirman que el dictador pretendía así que el país tuviera el mismo huso horario que la Alemania de Hitler. Geográficamente, a España le correspondería, como ha apuntado el economista Santiago Niño Becerra, estar en el GMT+0 (Greenwich Mean Time o Hora Media de Greenwich), como Reino Unido o Portugal. El cambio de hora siempre genera debate en España entre los ciudadanos e incluso entre los expertos. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, se mostraba contrario a mover el reloj. "Cambiar la hora dos veces al año ya no tiene sentido. Apenas ayuda a ahorrar energía y tiene un impacto negativo en la salud y en la vida de la gente", comentó. El líder del Ejecutivo incluso avanzó que trasladaría esta reflexión a los organismos competentes en la Unión Europea. Por ahora, no hay acuerdo entre los países miembros.

articles.title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
articles.summary: Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as
articles.body: Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to knowJio IPOThe IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota. Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: SBI data leak: Nearly 4,000 customer records found on dark web; what we know so far
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The State Bank of India (SBI) on Wednesday said that it has identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The State Bank of India (SBI) on Wednesday said that it has identified 3,897 customer records containing personally identifiable information (PII) in data suspected to have been exposed on the dark web. The bank has launched a detailed investigation to establish the authenticity, source and extent of the alleged exposure.In an exchange filing, the country's largest lender said it received alerts about the suspected exposure on October 16 from its Threat Intelligence Service Provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In. A preliminary analysis of approximately 3,75,000 records available on the dark web found 3,897 records containing PII.“During the preliminary analysis of approximately 375,000 records available on the dark web, 3,897 customer records containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) were identified. The exposed information reportedly included customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs, and metadata associated with loan/lead records and other related files,” the bank stated.SBI said it had activated its cyber incident response and containment protocols and engaged an independent cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In to assess the alleged compromise and the potential risks to customers and the bank.The lender clarified that the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, and that its core functions continued to operate normally.Names, addresses and loan records: What the data containedThe information identified in the preliminary analysis reportedly included customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses and residential addresses. The records also contained branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs, metadata associated with loan and lead records, and other related files.The ongoing investigation will examine whether the data is authentic and complete, determine the potential source and extent of the exposure, and assess the risks associated with the incident. SBI said appropriate remedial and preventive measures were being implemented as required.What the hacker group has claimedThe bank's statement follows a claim by an unidentified hacker group operating under the name ‘Siriusim’ that it had obtained confidential customer information allegedly linked to SBI, including personal details, loan applications and account-opening documents.Cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 highlighted the claim in a post on social media platform X. According to the account, the group purportedly possessed around 3.8 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 PDF documents associated with the lender.The alleged dataset contained customers' personal information, residential addresses, loan applications, supporting documents and other application-related records. CyberPulse56 first reported the claim on October 16, saying Siriusim had presented the material as its first disclosure of the dataset.However, the authenticity and origin of the alleged exposure remain unverified.Business operations remain unaffectedSBI said it would continue to monitor the situation and take appropriate measures in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements. The independent cybersecurity agency's assessment is underway, with remedial and preventive measures being implemented as required."We wish to submit that this does not have any material impact on Bank’s Core business operations, financial performance or business continuity. The Bank’s core business functions continue to operate normally without disruptions. A detailed assessment is currently underway and appropriate remedial and preventive measures are being implemented as required," the lender said.The alleged exposure comes amid broader concerns over cybersecurity risks facing India's financial sector. Earlier this year, the Reserve Bank of India stepped up cybersecurity requirements for commercial banks.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SBI confirms data leak, appoints cybersecurity agency to conduct assessment
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The State Bank of India (SBI) has confirmed a data exposure involving customer information, identifying 3,897 records containing personally
articles.body: MUMBAI: The State Bank of India (SBI) has confirmed a data exposure involving customer information, identifying 3,897 records containing personally identifiable information (PII) in a preliminary analysis of around 375,000 records found on the dark web. The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on Oct 16.The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 375,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses. The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.In its notice to stock exchanges, SBI said the preliminary analysis had identified records containing customers' registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records and related files. A CIF identifier is a unique number banks use to maintain a customer's consolidated relationship and account information. Lead IDs typically identify prospective customers or applications in a bank's sales and lending processes.The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. It has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In, India's national cyber incident response agency, to conduct an independent assessment.SBI said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally. It said the assessment was underway and remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.A threat actor is an individual or group that carries out, or claims to carry out, a cyberattack or other malicious activity. The term does not by itself establish who is responsible or whether a claim of a breach is genuine. The dark web refers to parts of the internet that are not accessible through standard search engines and typically require specialised software or configurations to access. It is sometimes used to trade stolen information, although the appearance of data there does not, by itself, establish how it was obtained.PII refers to information that can identify a person, either directly or when combined with other details. Names, phone numbers, dates of birth and residential addresses can be used for identity theft, targeted phishing and other forms of fraud if exposed. Metadata associated with loan applications may also reveal information about a customer's dealings with a bank.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SpaceX profits skyrocket to $4.4 billion as revenue jumps 161%, AI business surges 830%
articles.summary: SpaceX's Super Intelligence business has become the biggest driver of the company's latest quarterly growth, helping Elon Musk's aerospace company report
articles.body: SpaceX's Super Intelligence business has become the biggest driver of the company's latest quarterly growth, helping Elon Musk's aerospace company report a net profit of $4.4 billion in the July-September quarter.Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, rising 161 per cent to $14.6 billion, while spending on infrastructure also increased sharply.The company's third-quarter results showed a turnaround from the year-ago period, when SpaceX recorded a net loss of $1.1 billion on revenue of $5.6 billion. Adjusted EBITDA, which measures operating performance, rose 306 per cent to $8.8 billion from $2.2 billion.The Super Intelligence (SI) business, covering computing infrastructure, models and software applications, generated $7.6 billion in revenue during the quarter. This was an 830 per cent increase from $813 million in the corresponding period last year.SpaceX said the segment added $6.7 billion in year-on-year revenue through its solutions and infrastructure. Growth was attributed to new cloud services agreements, the acquisition of Cursor and wider adoption of Grok products by enterprise customers and consumers.Starlink adds 1.6 million subscribers in three monthsConnectivity services, led by Starlink, remained another major source of revenue for SpaceX. The segment brought in $5.2 billion in the quarter, marking a 69 per cent increase from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Its operating income rose 99 per cent to $2.4 billion.Starlink's consumer subscriber base reached 13.6 million as of September 30, compared with 7.2 million a year earlier. It added 1.6 million subscribers during the quarter. Monthly average revenue per user rose to $69 from $66 in the previous quarter.Space-related activities contributed $1.8 billion in revenue, up 6 per cent year-on-year. SpaceX completed 12 customer launches during the July-September period.The company also reported that its first orbital Starship flight delivered 26 Starlink V3 satellites. The deployment added around 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch.Computing capacity expands as investment climbsSpaceX's expansion came with a steep rise in capital spending. Capital expenditure stood at $19.6 billion in the third quarter, against $6.9 billion in the same period last year, largely due to investment in computing infrastructure.The company's computing capacity reached 1.7 gigawatts by September 30, compared with 0.6 gigawatts a year earlier, as it continued building infrastructure for its Super Intelligence business.The chief financial officer said the company intended to pursue expansion while keeping its investments and balance sheet on a disciplined footing."We are building the infrastructure of the future with discipline--focused on capital efficiency, strong returns on invested capital, and maintaining a robust, investment-grade balance sheet--while moving with the velocity to capture the opportunity in front of us," the CFO said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas hoy, miércoles 21 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.standfirst: Precio de la luz se abarata un 24,83% este miércoles
articles.summary: Precio de la luz se abarata un 24,83% este miércoles
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad hoy, 146,97 €/MWh, muestra una notable disminución de 48,55 € respecto al día anterior, cuando se situó en 195,52 €/MWh. Este miércoles, los consumidores pueden beneficiarse de estos precios más bajos. A medida que avanza el día, es relevante identificar las horas más costosas y las más económicas para optimizar el consumo. Los precios de la luz alcanzan su punto más alto durante las horas de mayor demanda, especialmente a partir de la mañana y hasta la noche. Durante el día, las franjas horarias más relevantes son, concretamente, entre las 07:00 - 08:00 (226.09 €/MWh) y 20:00 - 21:00 (284.49 €/MWh), donde se concentran los valores máximos. Esta tendencia se mantiene con picos significativos en 21:00 - 22:00 (284.93 €/MWh) y 19:00 - 20:00 (255.14 €/MWh). El bloque de horas caras es notable entre 07:00 y 22:00, con valores que superan considerablemente los 200 €/MWh, lo que refleja la variación de precios en función de la demanda eléctrica. La luz es más barata durante las primeras horas del día y al mediodía, ofreciendo oportunidades significativas de ahorro. Con tarifas que alcanzan precios muy bajos, como 0.75 €/MWh y 0.95 €/MWh entre las 13:00 - 15:00 y un momento crítico a las 11:00 - 12:00 con 1.99 €/MWh, existe una ventana amplia de precios bajos en la que los consumidores pueden beneficiarse. Las franjas horarias más relevantes que destacan en este análisis son 11:00 - 12:00, 12:00 - 13:00, 13:00 - 14:00 y 14:00 - 15:00, sumando hasta cuatro horas consecutivas de ahorro considerable. La jornada destaca por una considerable fluctuación en los precios, con un notable incremento de tarifas en las horas centrales, lo que refleja la volatilidad y el impacto de la demanda en el costo de la electricidad. Este patrón puede ser clave para los consumidores al planificar su consumo energético y optimizar sus gastos.

articles.title: UK approves new gas field in the North Sea amid concerns about energy security
articles.summary: The UK government has approved the development of a major new gas field in the North Sea amid rising concerns globally about energy security and the effect of climate policies on energy bills.
articles.body: The UK government has approved the development of a major new gas field in the North Sea as the war in the Middle East deepens concerns about energy security globally. The Jackdaw gas field, located 150 miles east of Aberdeen in Scotland, “will start to supply gas to British homes and businesses from as early as the end of this month,” the government said in a statement announcing its decision to greenlight production. “The Jackdaw decision is expected to increase domestic gas production by around 6% at its peak – supporting the UK’s gas supply over its lifespan of up to 11 years, boosting our energy security, protecting hundreds of jobs and adding an estimated £2.9 billion ($3.8 billion) to the UK economy,” the statement added. The decision, which is likely to anger environmental campaign groups, comes three months after US President Donald Trump described Britain’s North Sea oil and gas reserves as “invaluable” and welcomed any potential plans to allow drilling. This is a developing story and will be updated.
